nodes.name: VLA policies
nodes.description: Vision-Language-Action policies, a type of generalist robotic manipulation model.

nodes.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
nodes.description: A method used to make preferences learnable for robotic policies.

nodes.name: Mixed training
nodes.description: A training strategy that combines different types of data or objectives.

nodes.name: Sequential adaptation
nodes.description: A training strategy where models are adapted sequentially.

nodes.name: Contextual prompts
nodes.description: Prompts that provide additional context to guide policy behavior.

nodes.name: Preference-only training
nodes.description: A training strategy focused solely on learning preferences.

nodes.name: LoRA
nodes.description: Low-Rank Adaptation, a technique mentioned in relation to preference-only training.

nodes.name: Procedural generation pipeline
nodes.description: A pipeline used to automatically instantiate tasks and their preference-conditioned variants, generating demonstrations, metrics, and metadata.

nodes.name: OMPL planner
nodes.description: An Open Motion Planning Library planner used to generate trajectories within the data generation pipeline.

nodes.name: Trajectory smoothing
nodes.description: A technique applied to generated trajectories within the data generation pipeline.

nodes.name: VLM grounding
nodes.description: A process used to select preference targets within the data generation pipeline.

nodes.name: VLM planner
nodes.description: A Vision-Language Model planner used for preference-conditioned task planning within the data generation pipeline.

nodes.name: VLM checker
nodes.description: A Vision-Language Model checker used to verify skill satisfaction within the data generation pipeline.

nodes.name: LIBERO-PeRM
nodes.description: A benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation, comprising five task suites and 312 preference-conditioned tasks with pipeline-generated, human-reviewed demonstrations.

nodes.name: LIBERO-SinglePref
nodes.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating single-preference learning.

nodes.name: LIBERO-PrefScale
nodes.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating preference learning efficiency and generalization across data sizes, tasks, and layouts.

nodes.name: LIBERO-PrefConflict
nodes.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating preference-preference and task-preference conflicts.

nodes.name: LIBERO-PrefCompose
nodes.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating multi-preference composition.

nodes.name: LIBERO-ComprePref
nodes.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating realistic preference-conditioned reasoning based on contextual language.

nodes.name: Preference satisfaction
nodes.description: A metric to evaluate how well a policy adheres to user preferences.

nodes.name: Task success
nodes.description: A metric to evaluate if the nominal task goal is completed.

nodes.name: No-preference retention
nodes.description: A metric to evaluate how well a policy retains performance on tasks without preferences.

nodes.name: Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM)
nodes.description: The field of study focusing on enabling robots to execute tasks in ways that align with individual user preferences, habits, and constraints.

nodes.name: Preference learning
nodes.description: The process by which embodied agents acquire user preferences from demonstrations or other signals.

nodes.name: Zero-shot personalization
nodes.description: The ability of policies to follow preferences without explicit preference data.

nodes.name: Preference generalization
nodes.description: The ability of learned preferences to apply across different layouts and tasks.

nodes.name: Preference composition
nodes.description: The ability of policies to combine multiple preferences.

nodes.name: Preference conflicts
nodes.description: Situations where multiple preferences or a preference and a task goal are in opposition.

nodes.name: Observable preferences
nodes.description: Preferences that can be expressed in language, instantiated without changing the original task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks.

nodes.name: Motion Preference
nodes.description: A type of observable preference that constrains the physical properties of the trajectory (Pmotion).

nodes.name: Skill Preference
nodes.description: A type of observable preference that alters the execution behavior of a specific skill (Pskill).

nodes.name: User Profile
nodes.description: A type of observable preference that uses a user profile or context to guide subtask-level semantic choices (Pprofile).

nodes.name: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models
nodes.description: Models that integrate vision, language, and action for robotic control.

nodes.name: Current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization.
nodes.description: Observation that existing Vision-Language-Action policies perform poorly when asked to follow preferences without prior preference data.

nodes.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) makes preferences learnable.
nodes.description: Finding that applying Supervised Fine-Tuning enables policies to learn and incorporate user preferences.

nodes.name: Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation.
nodes.description: Result indicating that a mixed training approach helps policies maintain performance on tasks without preferences more effectively than sequential adaptation.

nodes.name: Mixed training improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training.
nodes.description: Finding that mixed training, when combined with contextual prompts, leads to better task success and preference satisfaction than training solely on preferences.

nodes.name: Mixed training can weaken motion-preference learning.
nodes.description: Observation that while mixed training has benefits, it may negatively impact the learning of motion-specific preferences.

nodes.name: Preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult.
nodes.description: Conclusion that current methods still face significant challenges in applying learned preferences to new situations, breaking down complex preferences, and resolving conflicting preferences.

nodes.name: Broader layout diversity and matched no-preference data also help.
nodes.description: Finding that increasing the variety of layouts and providing corresponding no-preference data can improve policy performance.
